comparison: Perfect agreement on background claims (C1-C14). Both evaluations recognize these as well-established foundational concepts about immune cell trafficking across the BBB, appropriately supported by citations. No concerns raised by either evaluation.

Both support biological findings from CD4+ T-cell analysis (C25-C35). OpenEval notes some interpretations are speculative while peer reviewers implicitly accept all findings without challenge. OpenEval provides more nuanced assessment of mechanistic claims.
Complete agreement on limitations (C63-C66). Both evaluations affirm that limitations are transparently acknowledged and appropriately contextualized without undermining the tool's utility.

Divergent assessments of future applications (C67-C72). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting these are speculative without supporting data. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, treating them as reasonable extensions. OpenEval applies stricter evidence standards.

Strong agreement on broad applicability (C50-C55, C85-C86). Both affirm cross-species and cross-cell-type generalizability. OpenEval provides detailed technical assessment while peer review emphasizes practical utility across different immune cells.

Agreement on limitations of manual analysis (C15-C18). Both recognize these establish motivation for the study. Peer review explicitly validates the problem statement, while OpenEval connects these claims to demonstrated experimenter variability.

Agreement on novel capabilities and comparison to existing tools (C58-C60). Both support claims about limitations of existing tools and UFMTrack's advantages. Peer reviewers note lack of clear software alternatives in the field.

Agreement on experimental methods (C73-C79 overlap). Both evaluations accept methodological details as appropriate and well-documented. Peer review also covers training methodology (C80-C84) which OpenEval addresses separately in R3.

Agreement on eliminating experimenter bias and improving accuracy (C36-C37, C42-C44). Both affirm the comparison methodology. OpenEval emphasizes systematic error identification while peer review focuses on manual vs. software comparison. Peer R4 also includes time savings claims (C45-C47) that OpenEval addresses separately.

Agreement on model performance metrics (C21-C24). Both accept technical performance comparisons without challenge. OpenEval provides detailed analysis of AP values and frame misalignment sensitivity. Peer review implicitly accepts through 'convincing framework' assessment.

Agreement on detection efficiency and performance metrics (C3, C38, C40-C41). Both affirm 90% detection efficiency and validation against manual analysis. Peer R1 also covers time savings (C48-C49, C61-C62) that OpenEval addresses in separate results R5 and R6.

Partial overlap on time analysis (C45-C49, C61). OpenEval R6 focuses specifically on time savings with detailed quantitative analysis. Peer R1 groups these with broader performance claims, affirming time savings as important benefit alongside accuracy.

Partial overlap on flow-related observations (C19-C20). OpenEval groups these with broader limitations of manual analysis. Peer R11 treats them as descriptive observations of the experimental system, acknowledging flow as a challenge.

Partial overlap on training methodology (C80-C84). OpenEval R3 addresses model training and performance metrics. Peer R12 groups training details with broader experimental methods, accepting technical implementation without question.

Partial overlap on time analysis (C45-C47). OpenEval R6 provides comprehensive time savings analysis. Peer R4 includes these claims within broader manual vs. software comparison, emphasizing time savings as key benefit.

Minimal overlap on bias elimination (C4, C62). OpenEval R5 focuses on eliminating experimenter bias with detailed analysis. Peer R1 briefly touches on these within broader performance validation, emphasizing accuracy and time savings.

Minimal overlap on tracking capabilities (C56). OpenEval R9 emphasizes novel tracking under flow conditions. Peer R5 focuses on cross-species/cell-type generalizability, with only tangential connection through broad applicability theme.
